body: This was the week the AI supercycle had to prove itself. Four of the world’s largest companies — **Meta, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon** — reported Q1 2026 earnings within 80 seconds of each other on Wednesday evening. The question the market had been asking for months finally had data attached to it: **is the spend generating returns fast enough to justify the price?**. And yet, after the dust settled, **Meta fell 7% in after-hours trading, Microsoft dropped 3%, and Amazon followed. **Revenue came in at $107 billion, up 19% year-on-year**. The AI narrative held up here: search resilience, cloud acceleration, and a capex commitment of up to $190 billion for the year that investors read as confidence rather than concern. But the headline that unsettled investors was the capex update: $190 billion for 2026, up 61% from last year and a full $35 billion above what analysts had modelled.

# Here are the stock market's winners and losers of Big Tech's most critical earnings stretch. It's been the stock market's most critical week of earnings, and the Big Tech winners and losers have emerged. Apple reported after the closing bell on Thursday, following Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft releasing results on Wednesday. **Why:** Apple reported revenue of $111.2 billion, up 17% year over year and surpassing Wall Street's estimate of $109.6 billion. Meta's ballooning AI spending overshadowed its first quarter earnings strength and the stock move reflected it. The Facebook parent company told investors it now expects to spend $125 billion to $145 billion in 2026, a big jump from the $115 billion to $135 billion range they gave the quarter prior. Google's results wowed Wall Street with strength in its cloud business supporting AI spending. Amazon stock popped after the company reported strong cloud growth and offered a look at its AI chip business.

Big Tech earnings are setting the tone for markets as 128 S&P 500 companies report this week. Following the busiest week of first-quarter earnings season last week, it’s the second busiest week with 128 S&P 500 companies scheduled to report. According to FactSet, 84% of S&P 500 companies are reporting earnings above the consensus estimates, with 63% of companies having released results. Companies reporting and combining actual results with consensus estimates for companies yet to report, the S&P 500’s blended earnings growth rate for the quarter is 27.1% year-over-year, above the 13.2% expectations at the end of the quarter. The S&P 500 rose last week. Because technology companies are critical drivers of earnings growth and account for a significant percentage of the S&P 500’s market capitalization, the Magnificent 7 remains the group to watch this earnings season. Five of the Magnificent 7 reported results last week: Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Apple (AAPL).
